correctness.rationale: At a rate-a_e update of an r-member edge with m ones, the conditional increment of K has mean zero and second moment m(r−m). Hence LH is minus the weighted pair cut. Equality with −lambda H gives the exponential by the finite-state generator; conversely differentiating at zero for every initial state makes every cut of w−lambda vanish. Subtract the {i,j} cut from the two singleton cuts to recover 2(w_ij−lambda). Nonempty positive-rate edges of size at least two preclude the lambda=0 case under the stated hypotheses. Between absorption and nonabsorption the contrast is controlled by n−1≤H≤floor(n²/4); integrating the resulting survival bounds gives both time bounds. The bounded martingale gives the fixation probability, and K²=nK−H gives the moment identity. Independently recounted the example: for a minority pair in the Fano plane its unique joint line produces consensus or a minority line; the four singleton-intersecting lines produce a minority singleton or a nonline minority triple, since the complement of a line contains no line. A minority line has six mixed lines meeting it once, all yielding a minority pair. A nonline minority triple has three pair-intersecting lines and three singleton-intersecting lines; the former give a singleton or another nonline class and the latter give a pair. A minority singleton has three incident lines, yielding consensus at rate 2 and a line at rate 1. These counts give the frozen quotient exactly for every class, omitting within-class jumps from its exit rates. In K7 the size-k minority has k(7−k) active pairs, with half their rate for each sign before taking complements. Each displayed rational vector solves its negative-generator system with right-hand side one; absorption makes the system nonsingular. The first entries differ by 13/210 at equal unit rate per edge, not by a rescaled discrete-step comparison. The frozen verify.py and evidence were inspected, not executed; the quotient calculations here are analytic.

originality.rationale: The local proportional-copy rule and first-moment conservation are not original. The cited Kim et al. paper also contains a q=1 simultaneous edge-update variant (not just the node updates mentioned in the frozen discussion), but in the inspected result it is an annealed uniformly sampled model with a diffusion-approximation exit time, not the fixed weighted-codegree theorem or exact finite-design comparison. Neither the inspected primary statements nor the closest catalogue findings directly cover the quantified converse or the rate-matched exact pair-versus-triple separation. This is a bounded best-of-knowledge conclusion, not a priority claim.
residual_risks: A focused web search was unavailable; that is not evidence of absence. The structural comparison relies on the accessible primary passages and catalogue findings.
Earlier unindexed static hypergraph, coalescing-lineage, or equivalent cut-generator formulations are not exhaustively excluded.
A future bibliography revision should explicitly note the simultaneous q=1 variant in Kim et al.; this does not change the scope or truth of the reviewed finding.

value.rationale: The cut converse is an exact identifiability criterion, stronger than observing a decay from a selected initialization. The Fano witness compares two natural pair-balanced systems at the same rates on pairs, with edges of size at most three and no global reset. It demonstrates that even perfectly matching first and second moment trajectories cannot recover expected consensus time, while giving a directly usable finite benchmark.
